US_branch_force_note: Branch OOB checked: Enterprise CV-6 and Saratoga CV-3 are permanent losses; Wasp CV-7 survives. Cabot CVL-28 is campaign-out from 3-Feb torpedo damage. Truk force remains centered on 5 CV + 3 CVL while Princeton/Langley support Catchpole.

Japanese_night_attack.composition_working: Truk-based B5N/B6N-class radar/search/torpedo aircraft plus a small physically valid Marianas/Tinian G4M-class contribution; no new units spawned.
Japanese_night_attack.cue: 1-3 hour old submarine/RI/DF sector cue plus dusk search reports. Enough for an area-search attack, not a weapon-quality carrier fix.

US_night_defense.state: FULL ALERT after unexpectedly hard daylight resistance
US_night_defense.night_fighter_procedures: Post-GALVANIC radar/night-CAP procedures are task-force-wide rather than dependent on one carrier, but hardware and intercept reliability remain immature.
US_night_defense.radar_night_fighters_available_center: 6-10 distributed F6F-3N/F4U-2N-class detachments/slots across appropriate carriers
US_night_defense.surface_screen: Fast battleships remain with carrier groups because the historical Katori/Maikaze surface chase did not occur; this thickens AA and screening.
US_night_defense.limitation: Night interception is not airtight; historical Truk night-fighter radar failures remain a valid warning against over-crediting US capability.

centered_result.US_ship_hits: One Type-91-class torpedo hit on an outer-screen destroyer slot; ship becomes constructive total loss/sinks. No carrier hit centered.
centered_result.meaning: Improved Japanese cue converts into one real torpedo hit, but stronger US radar/night defense and denser screen keep the attack away from the carrier core.

Japanese_submarine_night.result: No satisfactory torpedo shot on a fast carrier. One boat maintains only intermittent contact and is forced off by ASW.
Japanese_submarine_night.effect: Sector information remains useful for aircraft, but submarine attack and continuous shadowing cannot both be achieved.

US_offensive_night_strike.historical_anchor: Enterprise VT-10 historically launched 12 radar-equipped TBFs and achieved a disproportionate share of HAILSTONE shipping hits.
US_offensive_night_strike.branch_result: NO equivalent 12-plane radar-bombing night strike centered because Enterprise is a permanent Branch loss and no paid replacement offensive night-bombing unit is present in the current ledger.
US_offensive_night_strike.allowed_activity: Night CAP, search/ASW, rescue/recovery and small harassment/navigation sorties only.
US_offensive_night_strike.effect: Remaining lagoon shipping and fixed facilities receive no historical Enterprise-style night hammer; they survive to face daylight Day 2.

dawn_state.Truk_air_defense: still functioning at reduced throughput; one precision AA channel reliable, secondary channel intermittent
dawn_state.US_carriers: all Truk-assigned flight decks operational; no Intrepid-style campaign-out damage centered
